cases.description: Triple leg-off: 'Bought back the short Puts on TSLA, the short calls and short Puts on COST' — three leg-offs across two symbols

input.rawHtml: Bought back the short Puts on TSLA, the short calls and short Puts on COST
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Most complex case: three leg-offs in one message across two symbols. TSLA PDS → buy-to-close the short PUT leg ($440 SELL). COST CDS → buy-to-close the short CALL leg ($910 SELL). COST PDS → buy-to-close the short PUT leg ($850 SELL). The COST positions form an earnings strangle (iron condor): CDS $905/$910 + PDS $855/$850, both opened on Dec 11 before COST earnings. Signal[0] matches TSLA, signals[1] and [2] match the two COST positions. symbol field used to distinguish TSLA vs COST signals.

cases.description: 'Bought back the short Calls on MSTR for $1 profit - 15 Contracts. Still in long Calls' — CDS leg-off with explicit qty and retention confirmation

input.rawHtml: Bought back the short Calls on MSTR for $1 profit - 15 Contracts.  Still in long Calls
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: 'Bought back the short Calls' = buy-to-close the SELL leg of CDS. 'Still in long Calls' explicitly confirms the BUY leg is retained — this is a LEG_OFF not a CLOSE. '15 Contracts' matches position quantity. The remaining position becomes a naked long call. No badges — Hariseldon's statements are always text-only for options.

cases.description: 'I bought back the short Calls on MSTR - holding the long Calls' — CDS leg-off, clean retention phrase

input.rawHtml: I bought back the short Calls on MSTR - holding the long Calls
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Simpler phrasing than legoff-adv-002 but identical structure. 'holding the long Calls' is the retention marker. 'I bought back' (first-person + bought back) = buy-to-close pattern. No price info — pure LEG_OFF intent. The BUY call leg stays open as a naked long CALL.

cases.description: 'Bought back the Short Calls on META for $1.50 Profit' — CDS leg-off, no explicit retention phrase

input.rawHtml: Bought back the Short Calls on META for $1.50 Profit
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: No explicit 'still in' or 'holding' phrase — the LEG_OFF intent is implied solely by 'Bought back the Short Calls'. When a spread is open and the message says 'bought back the short [type]', the system must infer this is a LEG_OFF (partial close) not a full CLOSE. The BUY leg stays open. This tests implicit LEG_OFF detection without a retention confirmation phrase.

cases.description: 'Bought back the short calls on NFLX for a $6 profit - now holding the long Calls' — CDS leg-off with profit and retention

input.rawHtml: Bought back the short calls on NFLX for a $6 profit - now holding the long Calls
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Position based on Hariseldon's actual NFLX CDS: '$1130/$1140 for $3.28 - 20 Contracts' (Oct 22). 'now holding the long Calls' explicitly confirms the long $1130 BUY leg is kept. '$6 profit' applies to the short SELL leg buy-to-close. After this LEG_OFF, the $1130 call becomes a naked long CALL position.

cases.description: 'Bought back the short Puts on TSM PDS' — PDS leg-off, close short PUT leg

input.rawHtml: Bought back the short Puts on TSM PDS -
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: PDS leg-off: 'Bought back the short Puts on TSM PDS'. Explicit strategy noun 'PDS' confirms the spread type. Short PUT = SELL leg (lower strike $180). Buying it back = buy-to-close. The BUY leg ($185 PUT) is retained as a naked long PUT. Trailing dash with no profit amount is common Hariseldon shorthand.

cases.description: 'Bought back the Puts I sold on NVDA for a .33 profit' — naked PUT position close (not a spread leg-off)

input.rawHtml: Bought back the Puts I sold on NVDA for a .33 profit -
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Different pattern: 'Puts I sold' references a prior sell-to-open action (SHORT PUT position). 'Bought back' = buy-to-close the entire short PUT position (full CLOSE, not a leg-off). This tests disambiguation: when only one position exists with a single SELL leg, 'bought back' closes it entirely. The phrase 'I sold' anchors the reference to the existing SHORT direction PUT position. '.33 profit' = credit received on open minus debit paid to close.

cases.description: 'Long META CDS $755/$765 for $3.64 - 10 Contracts' — standard CDS open, part 1 of leg-off → exit sequence

input.rawHtml: Long META CDS $755/$765 for $3.64 - 10 Contracts
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Part 1 of 3 (open → leg-off → exit). Standard CDS open: Long badge = bullish view, CDS = call debit spread, direction LONG. $755/$765 = BUY $755 CALL, SELL $765 CALL. Sets up position for the leg-off in legoff-adv-009.

cases.description: 'Bought back the short Calls on META holding the long Calls' — CDS leg-off, retain long calls (part 2 of sequence)

input.rawHtml: Bought back the short Calls on META holding the long Calls
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Part 2 of 3 (open → leg-off → exit). 'Bought back the short Calls' = buy-to-close the SELL leg ($765). 'holding the long Calls' = retention marker, confirms BUY leg ($755) stays open. This is a LEG_OFF, not CLOSE. Nearly identical to legoff-adv-003 (MSTR) but part of a documented 3-step sequence where the exit follows in legoff-adv-010.

cases.description: 'Exit META CDS at break-even' — CLOSE remaining long calls after leg-off (part 3 of sequence)

input.rawHtml: Exit META CDS at break-even
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Part 3 of 3 (open → leg-off → exit). After legoff-adv-009 bought back the short $765 calls, the position converted from CDS to naked CALL (targetStrategy=CALL) with only the long $755 calls remaining. Trader still says 'Exit META CDS' using the original strategy name — system must fuzzy-match to the CALL position by symbol.

cases.description: 'Bought back the short Puts on MSFT' — PDS leg-off WITHOUT 'PDS' keyword, must close SELL PUT leg (bt:inland-bandicoot regression)

input.rawHtml: Bought back the short Puts on MSFT
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Bug from bt:inland-bandicoot trade 4377ca77: LLM hallucinated targetStrategy='CALL' on PDS (both legs are PUTs), causing wrong leg (507.5P BUY) to be closed instead of 500P SELL. Unlike legoff-adv-006 (TSM PDS), this message does NOT contain the keyword 'PDS'. The system must detect the PDS position structure (both legs same option type) and deterministically close the SELL leg.

cases.description: 'Bought back the Short Puts on COST PDS - that is no-brainer' — PDS leg-off, close SELL PUT leg (bt:inland-bandicoot regression)

input.rawHtml: Bought back the Short Puts on COST PDS - that is no-brainer on this PDS
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Bug from bt:inland-bandicoot trade 969895cc: Same wrong-leg LEG_OFF as legoff-adv-011. Despite the message explicitly mentioning 'PDS', the LLM still set targetStrategy='CALL'. Both legs are PUT. Fix: deterministic routing for vertical spreads bypasses LLM entirely.
